A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the Overcooked Generalisation Challenge. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, support comparison despite substantial rewriting and reformatting.

before.justification: V2 reports original agent-training experiments, layout generalisation, partner cooperation, robustness analyses and implementation throughput measurements.

after.justification: V3 retains original experiments, updates their results and reports revised spatial tests and an additional evaluation of Jha et al.'s method.

M1.justification: Both versions retain sequential layout generation, the five mutation operations, MAPPO training and the same CNN-LSTM, SoftMoE-LSTM and CNN-S5 architectures. Appendix A.5 confirms unchanged architectural components; rewritten descriptions do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: V2 already evaluates rotations, mirroring and size variation. V3 explicitly extends the spatial tests to squeezed and squeezed-small layouts (Table 2). The five original Overcooked tasks and FCP/MEP partner populations remain.

E2.justification: V3 adds an evaluated comparator: retrained agents from Jha et al. (2025), with results reported in Section 6. The principal DCD comparators remain unchanged. However, Table 2 no longer includes the CNN-LSTM and CNN-S5 comparisons reported in v2.

E3.justification: The spatial evaluation changes from a 24-layout, three-architecture summary to a SoftMoE-only analysis grouped by spatial category. V3 reports 32 transformed layouts, although Figure 4 mentions 28 additional layouts, leaving the exact count ambiguous. Main training budgets, partner-population settings and evaluation metrics remain substantially unchanged.

E4.justification: The spatial-robustness analysis is substantially revised: v2's low-variation symmetry results are replaced by category-specific results showing substantial instability, including squeezed layouts. V3 also newly reports that roughly one-quarter of randomly generated training layouts are unsolvable. Existing cell-visit case studies and appendix training curves are retained.

E5.justification: Reported DCD training seeds increase from three to five (Appendix A.2; Tables 1 and 12). V3 explicitly identifies 95% confidence intervals in Table 1 and Figure 9, while retaining standard-deviation and standard-error reporting elsewhere. The explicit one-sided paired t-test description disappears, although the p < 0.05 claim remains.

E6.justification: Tables 1 and 12–15 contain extensive numerical revisions: SoftMoE-PAIRED's Table 1 reward changes from 9.52 to 13.12, and its Table 12 solved rate changes from 11.46% to 14.72%. Cross-play matrices expand, spatial-test results are replaced, and Jha et al.'s evaluation adds a return of 0.46 ± 2.6. Changed seed counts and test conditions preclude interpreting these as same-setting method improvements.

T1.justification: The Dec-UPOMDP definition, return and value-function equations, and architectural mathematics are retained. V3 clarifies the cooperative/shared-reward characterization without changing the formal model or adding proofs.

C1.justification: The benchmark contribution and claim that current DCD methods struggle remain. V3 removes the abstract's broader claim of being the first environment specifically designed and evaluated for DCD, and drops v2's contribution claim that greater general capability yields better zero-shot cooperation, emphasizing persistent joint-generalisation failures instead.

C2.justification: V2 rejects spatial non-invariance as an explanation for failure; v3 instead identifies spatial overfitting as a principal failure mechanism (Table 2; Sections 5.2 and 5.4). V3 adds interpretations involving unsolvable curricula, expert routing and diversity across seeds. The principal layout-size and partner-reasoning limitations remain.

D1.justification: V3 adds a project-page access link and explicitly documents the 20-point soup-delivery reward, while condensing generation instructions, including earlier explanations of border walls and wall-budget enforcement. Repository access, licensing, hardware, training times and most implementation and hyperparameter details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 substantially revises positioning around joint generalisation, explicitly contrasting OGC with Jha et al.'s test-layout augmentation approach in the introduction, related work and discussion. It adds citations including ZSC-Eval and removes v2's discussion of Fontaine et al.'s procedural Overcooked work and several broader human-cooperation references.

P1.justification: Most main-text sections are extensively rewritten. The separate Research Challenges section is absorbed into the narrative, related work is reorganised around the two generalisation axes, experiments become four numbered subsections with takeaways, and Discussion becomes a standalone section. The title is expanded and appendix organisation is streamlined.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to a single-column journal layout, with extensive resizing and relocation of displays. V3 replaces the appendix's circular-layout illustration with a broader main-text transformation diagram, restructures Table 2 around spatial categories and expands seed-comparison heatmaps. Most other diagrams and appendix training plots are retained.

improvement.justification: Five-seed evaluation, expanded spatial tests and clearer experimental organisation strengthen v3. However, revised evidence introduces reporting problems: Table 15 changes the PAIRED/FCP Cramped solved rate from 72.48 ± 6.14% to an implausible 77.71 ± 83.7%, and Table 13's listed SoftMoE-PAIRED rewards average 14.97 rather than Table 1's 13.12. These unresolved reliability issues prevent a confident net quality judgment.
